subject: Kwest: Dedicated capacity allocation and region justification
body:
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: Elena Marin <elena@kwest.ai>
Date: Tue, 02 Mar 2027 09:17:00 -0700
Subject: Kwest: Dedicated capacity allocation and region justification

Hi Ben / Karthik —

Kwest just returned a more detailed 12-week forecast (attached) and asked for a concrete dedicated-capacity proposal that we can include in the SOW. They're explicitly asking about a Singapore pilot, with long-term usage spreading across US and EU as well. They indicated a willingness to commit to a 12-month reserved pool if we can guarantee region-specific SLAs and a small burst buffer for holiday spikes.

Key asks from Kwest (summarized):
- Pilot: Singapore (apac) dedicated pool for POC (target go-live: May).
- Production: steady-state monthly qps across US/EU/APAC with peak multipliers in APAC (2.5x).
- Commitment: prefer a 12-month reserved tranche but open to a staged commit if we can show price/latency tradeoffs.

Attachments: kwest_demand_forecast.xlsx (demand by week), draft SOW V2.

Can you review and propose a recommended region split (US/EU/APAC), committed v burst sizing, and any operational caveats we should surface to procurement? If we can get a simple matrix (nodes / vGPU / burst % / expected latency SLO) I’ll share that with Elena and the procurement vendor.

Thanks — Kim

--
Kimberly Park
Account Executive, Enterprise
Redwood Inference
kimberly@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0124

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: Elena Marin <elena@kwest.ai>
Date: Tue, 02 Mar 2027 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Kwest: Dedicated capacity allocation and region justification

Kim / Karthik —

Thanks for the forecast. Quick read-through + initial numbers below (we'll refine after you confirm region priority):

Proposal (baseline week avg -> committed / burst):
- APAC (Singapore pilot): 16 vGPUs committed (NVIDIA H100 equivalent), 6 vGPUs burst (37%). Expected token throughput targeting 30k qps sustained; latency SLO 95th <= 220ms for 512 tokens.
- US: 10 vGPUs committed, 4 vGPUs burst (40%). Latency SLO 95th <= 180ms.
- EU: 8 vGPUs committed, 3 vGPUs burst (38%). Latency SLO 95th <= 200ms.

Why this split? The forecast shows APAC peak multipliers and their product team insisted on local KV cache to avoid cross-region RTTs. The Singapore pilot requires contiguous allocation so we should plan on a separate pool (not just regional routing) to prove latency.

Operational caveats:
- Warm-up & KV cache: initial pilot will have cold-cache penalty for the first 48 hours; plan for a brief grace window in the SOW.
- Burst credit: we can guarantee burst capacity for up to 10% of days in a 30-day window before we require scaled commit.
- Pricing: staged discount for commit (0–6 months 15% off list, 6–12 months 22% off if they convert to full reserve).

I'll build a small matrix and include rough cost delta per region. Want me to include a fallback plan (model variant routing to smaller instance types) if they push for lower price?

Ben
Principal Capacity Planner
Redwood Inference

-----------------------------

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.ai>
Cc: Elena Marin <elena@kwest.ai>
Date: Wed, 03 Mar 2027 08:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Kwest: Dedicated capacity allocation and region justification

Ben / Kim —

Thanks — this looks sensible. A couple of product/negotiation notes from my side: 

1) Prioritization: we should tie the APAC pilot to a small upfront tranche (4–6 months) and a conversion trigger. That reduces our risk for Singapore capacity while still giving Kwest runway to validate.
2) SLA exceptions: call out KV cache warm-up as a non-SLA-impacting event but offer a one-time credit if their production traffic experiences >2x latency above SLO in first 72 hours. Keeps politics simple.
3) Marketplace + procurement: Elena mentioned they may buy via CloudProcure. If so, we'll need a clear SKU mapping and a DocuSign-ready SOW. Ask Finance to pre-approve the SKU/price mapping for the committed nodes — otherwise procurement will ask for multiple iterations.

If we get buy-in on staged commit + credit guardrail, I can approve the price bands on the deal and push legal to lock the SOW language.

Karthik
VP, Dedicated Solutions
Redwood Inference

-----------------------------

From: Elena Marin <elena@kwest.ai>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, CloudProcure <ops@cloudprocure.com>
Date: Thu, 04 Mar 2027 10:09:00 +0800
Subject: Re: Kwest: Dedicated capacity allocation and region justification

Thanks Kim, Ben, Karthik —

Appreciate the quick turnaround. A few clarifications from Kwest: 
- The Singapore pilot is a hard requirement; timeline is May 10th for internal demo.
- We'd prefer an initial 6-month commit for APAC with an option to extend to 12 months; pricing and conversion terms you suggested sound workable but please include the credit guardrail in writing.
- Procurement (we looped in CloudProcure) wants the following on the SOW: exact SKU(s), node count by month, latency SLOs, list of blackout windows for maintenance, and an explicit burst policy.

We attached an updated weekly profile to the forecast with clearer ramp weeks (see kwest_demand_forecast.xlsx). Also please review the SOW_draft_v2.pdf (we flagged the pilot dates and requested the credit clause) — we can accept DocuSign once you return a final SOW.

Elena Marin
Head of Product Ops
Kwest AI
elena@kwest.ai | +65 8123 4456

Attachment stubs: kwest_demand_forecast.xlsx (spreadsheet, 42KB), SOW_draft_v2.pdf (pdf, 176KB)

Subject: Re: Kwest: Dedicated capacity allocation and region justification

Elena / team —

Nice — we can do the staged 6-month APAC commit with a conversion to 12 months. Ben will send a regionized SKU matrix and cost delta by EOD Monday. Karthik and I will work with Legal to bake the warm-up credit clause into the SOW and prepare a DocuSign-ready version.

Action items:
- Ben: SKU matrix + cost delta (US/EU/APAC) — deliverable: Monday, 8 Mar EOD PST.
- Karthik: approve price band and sign-off language for SOW credit clause.
- Kim (me): consolidate SOW and route to CloudProcure for procurement mapping.

I'll keep you posted and attach the DocuSign link once Legal finalizes the SOW.

Thanks everyone — Kim
